site.title: Jika Tabi
site.tagline: Split-toe tabi and work boots, sewn to the last.

categories.name: Shop notes
categories.description: The shop, the arch and the fittings.

posts.title: Eight stitches to the centimetre
posts.excerpt: Every seam on a pair of jika-tabi is sewn on the wooden last, eight stitches to the centimetre, in cotton thread.
posts.content:
Every seam on a pair of jika-tabi is sewn on the wooden last, eight stitches to the centimetre, in cotton thread.

Why the last

Sewing on the last means the upper takes the shape of a foot before it ever meets one. The split between the toes is the hardest seam, and the slowest.

A pair that puckers at the split is unpicked and sewn again.

posts.title: Why we dye canvas fifteen times
posts.excerpt: Our indigo canvas goes into the vat fifteen times before it reaches the cutting table, so it fades slowly and evenly.
posts.content:
Our indigo canvas goes into the vat fifteen times before it reaches the cutting table.

Fading well

A light dye fades in patches where the foot bends. Fifteen dips build the colour deep into the thread, so a three-year-old pair is lighter, not blotchy.

posts.title: White tabi for the stage
posts.excerpt: Each autumn a theatre down the line orders forty pairs of white tabi. Here is how we fit a whole cast in a day.
posts.content:
Each autumn a theatre down the line orders forty pairs of white tabi.

A day of feet

The cast comes in two at a time. We trace, measure the split and try a sample last, and the stage manager writes each size on a paper tag.

posts.title: A new sole on an old pair
posts.excerpt: A pair from 1987 came back last week for its fourth sole. The upper is soft as a glove and good for years yet.
posts.content:
A pair from 1987 came back last week for its fourth sole.

Keeping the upper

We cut the old rubber away, clean the canvas and press a new sole on by hand. The pair goes home a day later, quieter than it arrived.
